ratings_why.fun: Gust Page and Sir Vane win early fights, the Gale turns fights into shop stats from turn 2, and Lady High Pressure's favourite board is a capstone I'd climb towards.
ratings_why.distinct: Defer, which turns a weak unit's attack into your favourite's extra swing, and a fight count that pays out in the shop are fresh; the extra attacks on their own are Windfury in new clothes.

verdict_why: Mostly playable now, but Sir Vane's mirror case needs a ruling and which unit counts as the favourite fights the Defer plan.

points.text: Two Sir Vanes, or Vane against a side with more units, leaves 'your side attacks first' unresolved. Give a tiebreak in the text, such as 'if both sides would, the side with more units goes first'.

'Biggest' counts Health, so Old Föhn (2/11), The Helm and Bowing Zephyr often become the favourite and Gust for 1 or 2 Attack. Having Defer pick 'your highest-Attack other unit' would make the favourite the hitter the plan wants.

Permanent growth stops climbing late: Cirrus Steward caps at +4/+4 and Mackerel Sky at +2/+2, and no Tier 6 unit grows the board across turns. One Tier 6 unit that turns a big Gale into permanent stats would give the late game a curve to chase.
Bowing Zephyr has nobody to Defer to on turns 2 and 3. Pine-Cone Augur and Gust Page carry the early game alone, so a Tier 2 body that makes a Gust on its own would smooth the start.
Gale Warnings stay forever and stack, so a board that holds Gale 8 or more adds one more permanent Gust every turn. That's a fun high roll; say whether it is meant to keep stacking without end.

standouts.why: Lady High Pressure turns the whole board into one favourite's queue of Gusts, a real capstone the comp is built to reach.
Gust Page is a clean Tier 1 tempo body that starts the Gale on turn 1.
Windhover makes seating a puzzle: who sits on its left decides who swings twice.

weakest.why: Bowing Zephyr is a 1/5 that does nothing until you have a favourite worth deferring to.
Red Sky at Night is plain economy with a small body, and it pays most when you're already winning.
The Helm's Shield on the biggest unit is fine but has no hook of its own beyond Defer.

flags.note: Gale Warnings add a permanent Gust each turn the Gale holds 8 or more, which keeps the Gale at 8 or more. Linear, but it never stops.
With Lady High Pressure, Old Föhn soaks every Gust's return damage, so a favourite only gets hurt by enemy attacks. Bog folk and random damage are the counterplay.
Lord Mistral, Mistral Outrider and Windhover chain many Gusts in one fight. Each has a cycle limit, so it's in-fight only, but the fallback cap may be needed.
Two sides that both 'attack first' have no ruling.
